newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Speculation in financials lifts Brussels Bel-20.
newsitem.headline: Speculation in financials lifts Brussels Bel-20.

text.p: Talk Dutch financial services group ING was interested in buying Belgian insurer Royale Belge bolstered a whole collection of Belgian shares on the Brussels bourse on Thursday, dealers said.

The collective gains helped the Bel-20 index .BFX remain just in the black at the end of a mixed session, ending up 1.22 points at 2,374.81. Dealers said dollar strength and firmer bonds meant further gains were possible, although late afternoon slippage could put a brake on the market's advance.
"Sentiment is still good," a trader said. But another noted, "For a lot of analysts 1997 targets have already been met."
The Bel-20 has already risen some 500 points this year, breaching 2,300 in June, a level set by some analysts as their target for the year.

Background worries about the timing of the next increase in U.S. interest rates and the shape of economic and monetary union in Europe could keep the bourse from making much more headway, dealers said.

Among financials Royale Belge gained 200 francs at 10,200 on the talk of an ING appetite. Shareholder GBL advanced 190 francs to 6,080, while holding company Sofina, which also holds a Royale Belge stake, rose 575 francs to 26,500.

The talk said a Royale Belge purchase by ING would raise ING's stake in Belgian bank BBL from some 20 percent to 30 percent since with RB ING would gain access to BBL stock. This aspect of the rumour boosted BBL 70 francs to 9,220.
Reuter calls to GBL and Royale Belge for comments were not returned.
Elsewhere in the banking sector Kredietbank ended a spell of profit-taking after merger speculation faded, gaining 100 francs at 14,425.
